title: CI: act replays give all matrix legs the same four CPUs; give each concurrent container its own
issue_body:
## Problem

A local act replay of a PR takes about 4 hours, while the hosted run takes about 2. The cause is the replay's CPU shape, not the work.

- `scripts/act_ci.py` `container_cpuset()` gives every job container of a replay the same `--cpuset-cpus` range: `0-3` on slot 0, and `4N` to `4N+3` on slot N (`CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT = 4`).
- act 0.2.89 runs a matrix job's legs `strategy.max-parallel` wide, 4 by default, and `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT = 1` keeps one job at a time. So `rtl-full`'s sharded jobs run up to four legs at once, all on the same four CPUs.
- On the hosted service, each leg has its own 4-vCPU runner. The replica therefore gives each leg about a quarter of a hosted runner's CPU, while the rest of a 128-vCPU host stays idle. During PR #721's replay on 2026-10-12, the host load was 4 to 7.
- The isolated slots (#532) work: `--interrupt-selftest --slot 1` passed on 2026-10-12, with a memory peak of 20.7 GiB against the 24G cap and the cap hit 0 times. Each slot still has only four CPUs for all its legs.

## Acceptance

1. **Each concurrent container gets its own CPUs.** Each job container that runs concurrently in a replay gets a `--cpuset-cpus` range of its own, `CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT` wide, so a leg sees what a hosted runner gives it. Ranges never overlap within a slot or across slots. The per-container memory bound and the slot memory cap are unchanged. A host without enough CPUs is a Refusal, as today.
2. **Derived, not mirrored.** The number of ranges a slot needs comes from the replayed workflows' concurrency (`max-parallel` and `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT`), not from a mirrored constant. The self-test proves the ranges are disjoint at the maximum concurrency.
3. **Fidelity.** No workflow, step or job changes. Each leg still sees `nproc` = 4. The replay's verdict on the same PR head is unchanged.
4. **Measured.** One `rtl-full` replay at a known head, before and after, records the wall clock per job and the slot memory peak. The change reports the result as measured.
5. **Optional, measured separately.** `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT` 2 within the slot memory cap, kept only if the cap is not hit.

scope_and_evidence_comments.body:
[A10] **Lane assignment.** Executor [A607], branch `730-act-cpusets` from dev `dc4d06cb`. Internal review R632, external review R633. The maintainer asked for faster CI (2026-10-12, "ok improve ci").

1. Implement acceptance 1–3 in `scripts/act_ci.py`, with the self-test and documentation that already cover `container_cpuset`, the slots and the replica shape (`docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` or wherever these are documented). Keep every existing ownership, lease, cleanup and Refusal guarantee. The existing self-tests (`--selftest`) still pass. Add the disjointness proof with a planted overlap that fails.
2. **Measure (acceptance 4).** Replay PR #728 (open, head `2c2f3369`) with `--workflow rtl-full --sudo --slot 3` twice, one run after the other: first with dev's `act_ci.py`, then with the lane's. Record the per-job wall clock and the slot memory peak for both. Start each as a background job with its own log, and poll it. Never run more than one replay at a time from this lane. Use slot 3 only; slots 1 and 2 belong to the manager's queue.
3. **Optional acceptance 5** runs only after item 2, and only if the slot memory cap was not hit.

STOP on any of these: a guarantee would have to weaken; a workflow file would have to change; the after replay's verdict differs from the before replay's.

Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A10] **Round 2.** R633-1 ([6132335284](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/731#issuecomment-6132335284), four MAJOR) and R632-1 ([6132397037](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/731#issuecomment-6132397037), two MINOR) are NEGATIVE. All findings are accepted. Executor [A607].

1. **R633-1-F1: a reservation lives until destroy.** A range stays reserved to its container from placement until the container's `destroy` event, or until an inspect proves the container gone. A `die` does not free it, because a stopped container keeps its cpuset and can restart. Handle delayed and out-of-order lifecycle events by checking each container's effective cpuset with `docker inspect`, not by counting events. Correct the summaries and the documented guarantee. Add a standing test for R633-1's sequence (`create A, update A, start A, die A, create B, update B, start B, start A`): A and B must never hold one range.
2. **R633-1-F2: an uncertain update stays reserved.** A failed or timed-out `docker container update` keeps its target range reserved until an inspect shows the container's effective cpuset. A failed command never counts as proof that the container stayed on staging. Keep the existing split between resource uncertainty, which is a warning, and a candidate verdict. Add a standing test for R633-1's probe: the update is applied on the daemon, then the CLI times out.
3. **R633-1-F3: slot 0 refuses too.** Acceptance 1 stands: a host without the CPUs for the derived ranges is a Refusal on every slot, slot 0 included. Remove the silent fallback, and align the self-test and the documentation.
4. **R633-1-F4 and R632-1-F1: cleanup order.** A failure in `terminate_group`, or any cleanup step, must not skip the reader completion and dead-thread proof or the stream containment. Keep the original failure and block the Docker boundary's teardown until those obligations are met. Add a self-test that fails when the reader join is missing, as R632-1-F1 asks, and one for R633-1's injected reaping failure.
5. **R632-1-F2.** Pin at run level that a container left on staging prints a warning and never changes the run's verdict.
6. **Residue.** Apply R632-1-R1 (mixed runner versions in the authoritative doc) and R632-1-R2 (the slot-0 sentence in the PR body, now superseded by item 3).

The ruling 6131815815 still holds: no replay against a live PR, only `--selftest` and `--dry-run`. Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A607] REVIEW READY (Round 2)
Commit: `5ba8313a3f036f34aac1a6bfbfcec0e0efd8c646` on `730-act-cpusets`. These are new commits on top of `eb566634`, with no rebase or amend. They are local and not pushed: this round may not push.
- `93215f07`: code and self-tests.
- `5ba8313a`: `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`.

Changed (answers to [6132404197](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/730#issuecomment-6132404197), items 1-6):
1. **R633-1-F1.** A job range is reserved from placement until the container's `destroy`, or until `docker container inspect` shows the daemon no longer has it. `die` frees nothing. Where a container runs is read with `docker container inspect --format {{.HostConfig.CpusetCpus}}`, not inferred from events. The runner reads it after each move, at each `start`, at an `update` of a container not yet seen on its range, and for every holder when no range is free.
   - Standing test `selftest_job_cpu_record`: R633-1's exact sequence `create A, update A, start A, die A, create B, update B, start B, start A` runs against a model daemon that holds each container's real cpuset. After every event, no two containers share a range, and every container on a job range holds it in the record. A restarts on `4-7`; B gets `8-11`.
2. **R633-1-F2.** The target is reserved before `docker container update` runs. A timeout or failure keeps it reserved, and then an inspect decides. On target, the container counts as moved, with a warning saying the command failed but inspect shows it there. Off target or unreadable, it is a warning, and the range stays reserved until removal. Only the daemon's `No such container` frees it. A late `update` event is re-read.
   - Standing test `selftest_job_cpu_move_failures`, each case with the next container created while the outcome is uncertain: applied then CLI timeout (R633-1's probe); lost, then landing late; move and read both timing out; refused.
   - Problems stay warnings and never reach a verdict.
3. **R633-1-F3.** Slot 0 refuses a host without the derived ranges, as every slot does. The fallback and its plan text are gone. The self-test checks slot 0 at 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 19, 20 and 21 CPUs for one and four containers: 19 refuses and 20 gives `4-7`..`16-19`; 7 refuses and 8 gives `4-7`.
4. **R633-1-F4 and R632-1-F1.** `stop_job_cpu_range_monitor` runs poll, containment, reader join and pipe close whatever an earlier step raised, and raises the first failure only after all of them. The join is retried until the reader is proven ended. A reader still alive after the bounded wait is a warning plus a printed containment hold, and teardown waits.
   - Standing test `selftest_job_cpu_monitor_busy`: the stream's line arrives only after the body returns, the move takes 0.2 s, and the stream ends only once contained. It runs for return, raise, SIGTERM, R633-1's reap failure, and raise plus reap failure.
   - Also pinned: poll failure, a join that fails once, and a stream or reader that cannot start.
5. **R632-1-F2.** `selftest_cpu_range_warnings` drives `execute_workflows` through the real spawn boundary with a container left on staging and two planted problems. With act exit 0 the verdict is `PASS`; with exit 3 it is `FAILED (3)`. Each workflow prints its summary once and exactly one `WARNING ... CPU ranges:` line per problem.
6. **Residue.** R632-1-R1's mixed-runner sentence is in CI_WORKFLOWS.md's slot resource bounds. R632-1-R2 is superseded by item 3, and the PR body now states the refusal.

Also found and fixed: `docs.yml` runs `act_ci.py --selftest` on a 4-vCPU hosted runner. Three self-test harnesses used the real CPU count and would have refused there under item 3. They now pin 128 CPUs.

The summary line changed, and the post-merge reading uses it: `act-ci: <wf>: CPU ranges: <n> job container(s) created: <m> seen on a range of their own by docker inspect, <g> removed before that, <s> never seen on one; at most <k> held a range at once`. For a full `rtl-full` run, expect `m == n`, `g == s == 0`, `k == 4`, and no `WARNING ... CPU ranges:` line. The plan line, the per-slot layout and the disjointness proof are unchanged.

Validation (all rc 0 at `5ba8313a`; CPython 3.12.3, PyYAML 6.0.3, pinned Markdown renderer):
- `python3 scripts/act_ci.py --selftest`: PASS, 490 ok, 0 FAIL (was 477). It also passes on CPython 3.14.7, and with `os.cpu_count` stubbed to 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 19, 20, 39, 40 and 128.
- `python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check`: 2016 items. `--selftest`: 2828 arms.
- `scripts/act_slot_proof.sh --selftest`: 44 cases.
- `python3 scripts/check_py_idiom.py`: ratchets hold (long function 9 <= 9, parameters 7 <= 7, over-long 0). `--selftest` also passes.
- `python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --check` and `--selftest`.
- `python3 scripts/docs_check.py`, `python3 scripts/check_doc_style.py`, `python3 scripts/gen_toc.py --check` and `--verify-anchors`, and `python3 scripts/check_doc_paths.py`.
- `python3 scripts/check_em_dash.py --base dc4d06cb`: 0 findings over 120 added lines.
- `git diff --check dc4d06cb HEAD`.
- Mutants on scratch copies of the head tree:
  - 21 of 21 Round 2 mutants killed. They include `die` freeing, a timed-out or refused move released, no inspect, reap failure skipping the join, join before containment, a failed join not retried, the slot-0 fallback restored, and the harness host unpinned.
  - R632-1's `mutants.py`, re-run: 19 killed, including M13, M16, M17 and M23.
  - M18 survives; only the live interrupt gate pins it.
  - M08, M09, M20 and C24 are no longer applicable, because their anchors were removed by this round.
- Offline dry run of the shipping `rtl-full`: slot 0 and slot 3 rc 0, with plan lines byte-identical to Round 1.

Acceptance criteria:
- 1: met in code, proven offline, now with slot 0 refusing too.
- 2: met.
- 3: no workflow, step or job change, and every range is 4 wide. The same-head verdict comparison is post-merge (ruling).
- 4 and 5: post-merge (ruling).
- Hence `Relates to #730`.

Open risks/questions:
- **Material decision on item 2.** A timed-out move whose inspect shows the staging range keeps its target reserved until `destroy`, not just "until an inspect shows the effective cpuset". The daemon may still apply that request, and releasing the range would let the late completion land on a range already given to the next container (R633-1's delayed-completion case). The cost is one idle range for that container's life, reported as a warning. If the manager wants release on the first inspect instead, that is a one-line change, and the "lost then landing late" arm would then fail by design.
- No `docker events`, `docker container update` or `docker container inspect` has run against a live daemon in this lane (ruling). Each container now costs one inspect after its move and one at each `start`. The added latency is not measured.
- `--dry-run` is still not daemon-free (unchanged from Round 1). The dry-run lines come from the offline harness.

[A607]

## Contents

- **[Status](#status)**: Green/WIP/blocked, test tally, and `branch` -> `dev`.
- **[Linked Issue / roles](#linked-issue--roles)**: Public task, executor, and independent reviewers.
- **[Description](#description)**: What changed and why.
- **[Authoritative references](#authoritative-references)**: Requirements/specification clauses and docs.
- **[How to get into the same state](#how-to-get-into-the-same-state)**: Copy-pasteable checkout/dependency/environment commands.
- **[How to validate](#how-to-validate)**: Exact reviewer commands and expected result.
- **[Known limitations / out of scope](#known-limitations--out-of-scope)**: What this deliberately does not do, and why.
- **[Definition of Done](#definition-of-done)**: The merge bar from [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Status

GREEN: `act_ci.py --selftest` 490/490 arms; every gate below rc 0 at `5ba8313a`.
`730-act-cpusets` -> `dev`.

## Linked Issue / roles

Relates to #730

Acceptance 1 and 2 are met. Acceptance 3 is met except its "verdict unchanged on the same
head" clause; 4 and 5 are not done here. By the ruling on #730 there are no replays in this
lane, and the manager measures after the merge. So this PR does not close the Issue.

Executor: `[A607]`
Internal cleared-context reviewer: `[R632]`
External reviewer: `[R633]`

## Description

act 0.2.89 gives every job container of a run one `--container-options` word. A replay
therefore put all of a matrix job's concurrent legs on the same four CPUs (`0-3` on slot 0,
`4N..4N+3` on slot N), a quarter of a hosted runner each. An interrupted `rtl-full` replay
on slot 3 showed four Verilator legs, every one with `cpuset.cpus` `12-15`, using about 1 CPU
each.

| Piece | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Derivation | `job_container_width` and `replay_container_concurrency` (`scripts/act_ci.py`). A matrix job runs its literal `max-parallel` containers at once, or act's default 4 when it names none. A job without a matrix runs one. A workflow's concurrency is its `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT` widest jobs added up. An unreadable `max-parallel` is a Refusal. Shipping `rtl-full` derives 4; `docs`, `elaborate` and `rtl-fast` derive 1. |
| Layout | `slot_cpu_base`, `container_cpuset` and `job_cpu_ranges`. Slot N owns CPUs `20N..20N+19`: a staging range, then `SLOT_JOB_RANGES` job ranges. `SLOT_JOB_RANGES` is `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT` x act's default width, which is 4, and each range is `CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT` (4) wide. Slot 0 stages on `0-3` and uses `4-7`, `8-11`, `12-15` and `16-19`. Slot 3 stages on `60-63` and uses `64-67` to `76-79`. A run uses only the ranges it derives, and a run that derives more than 4 is refused. A host without the CPUs for the ranges a run derives refuses the run before the slot is entered, on every slot, slot 0 included: 20 CPUs for `rtl-full` on slot 0, and 8 for a workflow that derives one container. |
| Placement | `JobCpuRanges` and `job_cpu_range_monitor`. While act runs, a `docker events` stream filtered to the run's ownership label runs in its own session. At each job container's `create`, the monitor reserves the lowest free job range and moves the container there with `docker container update --cpuset-cpus`. A reservation lasts until the container's `destroy`, or until `docker container inspect` shows the daemon no longer has it. A `die` frees nothing, because a stopped container keeps its cpuset and can start again. A move that failed or timed out keeps its range reserved, because the daemon may have applied it or may still. Where a container runs is read with `docker container inspect`, never inferred from events: after each move, at each `start`, at an `update` of a container not yet seen on its range, and for every holder when no range is free. |
| Shutdown | On every exit the stream's process group is walked down the containment ladder, and the reader is joined and proven ended before the Docker boundary's teardown. A failed poll, containment, leader reap, join or pipe close does not skip any later step. The first failure is raised only after all of them, and a reader still running after its bounded wait is printed as a containment hold. |
| Reporting | Before the boundary, the run prints its plan (below). After each workflow it prints `CPU ranges: <n> job container(s) created: <m> seen on a range of their own by docker inspect, <g> removed before that, <s> never seen on one; at most <k> held a range at once`. Each problem is a separate warning line. A container left on the staging range never changes a verdict: it keeps `nproc` 4. |
| Interrupt gate | `--interrupt-selftest` runs its job under the monitor and requires the job's container to be seen on a range of its own. |
| Unchanged | No workflow, step, job, suite, RTL or firmware file. Unchanged: `--memory=16g --memory-swap=16g`, `--concurrent-jobs 1`, the 24G slot cap, the ownership label, leases, cleanup and every existing Refusal. |
| Docs | `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`: replica shape, reservations, slot resource bounds (including mixed runner versions), the interrupt gate, and the self-test lists. |

Dry run of the shipping `rtl-full` (the real dry-run code path with GitHub, git, the slot daemon
and the Docker boundary stood in; the same lines are a self-test arm):

```text
act-ci: job container CPUs: up to 4 at once (max-parallel, CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT 1); each created on --cpuset-cpus=0-3, then moved to a free one of --cpuset-cpus=4-7 --cpuset-cpus=8-11 --cpuset-cpus=12-15 --cpuset-cpus=16-19
act-ci: job container CPUs: up to 4 at once (max-parallel, CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT 1); each created on --cpuset-cpus=60-63, then moved to a free one of --cpuset-cpus=64-67 --cpuset-cpus=68-71 --cpuset-cpus=72-75 --cpuset-cpus=76-79
```

The first line is slot 0 and the second is slot 3.

Disjointness proof (`selftest_cpu_layout_disjoint`): every slot from 0 to 63 runs 4 job
containers at once, giving 320 ranges, each 4 wide, with no shared CPU. It fails on two planted
overlaps:

- across slots, the pre-#730 `slot * 4` spacing (`slot 0 job range 0 and slot 1 staging share
  CPU 4`);
- within a slot, every leg on one range.

A staging range planted onto a job range is refused at run time.

### Round 2 (answers R633-1 and R632-1)

| Finding | Fix | Standing self-test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R633-1-F1: `die` freed a range a stopped container keeps | Reservation until `destroy` or an inspect proving the container gone; placement read by inspect | `selftest_job_cpu_record` runs R633-1's sequence `create A, update A, start A, die A, create B, update B, start B, start A` against a model daemon that holds each container's real cpuset. After every event, no two containers share a range, and every container on a job range holds it in the record. |
| R633-1-F2: a failed or timed-out update freed its target | The target is reserved before the update and stays reserved whatever the command reports. Only the daemon's `No such container` frees it. | `selftest_job_cpu_move_failures` covers four cases, each with the next container created while the outcome is uncertain: applied then CLI timeout (R633-1's probe); lost then landing late; move and read both timing out; refused. Every warning text is pinned. |
| R633-1-F3: slot 0 fell back silently | Slot 0 refuses like every slot | `selftest_job_cpu_ranges` checks slot 0 at 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 19, 20 and 21 CPUs for one and four containers. |
| R633-1-F4, R632-1-F1: a reap failure skipped the join; no arm saw a missing join | Each shutdown step runs whatever an earlier one raised; the join is retried until the reader is proven ended | `selftest_job_cpu_monitor_busy`: the reader is still moving a container when the body returns, and the stream ends only once contained. It runs for return, raise, SIGTERM, reap failure, and raise plus reap failure. Also covered: poll and join failures, and start failures. |
| R632-1-F2: verdict invariance not pinned at run level | No runtime change | `selftest_cpu_range_warnings` drives `execute_workflows` with a container left on staging and two problems. With act exit 0 the verdict is `PASS`; with exit 3 it is `FAILED (3)`. Each workflow prints its summary once and exactly one warning per problem. |
| R632-1-R1, R2 | The mixed-runner-version sentence is in the authoritative doc, and the slot-0 sentence above is replaced | Docs gates |

Also fixed while checking item 3: three self-test harnesses called `run_validation` with the
host's real CPU count. The hosted `docs` job runs the self-test on a 4-vCPU runner, so those
harnesses would have refused there. They now pin 128 CPUs. The self-test passes with 1, 2, 3, 4,
7, 8, 19, 20, 39, 40 and 128 simulated CPUs.

Mutation evidence at `5ba8313a`, on scratch copies of the tree, where each mutant must fail the
self-test:

- 21 of 21 Round 2 mutants are killed. They cover every fix above, plus the harness pin, the
  planted exit, and the held-range check.
- R632-1's own campaign, re-run here: 19 killed, including M13, M16, M17 and M23. M18 survives;
  it is pinned only by the live interrupt gate. Four mutants no longer apply, because their
  anchors were removed by this round: `die` freeing, the slot-0 fallback, and the old held-range
  line, now N21.

Material decision: an uncertain move keeps its range until the container is removed, even after
an inspect shows the container still on the staging range. The daemon may still apply the timed-out
request, and releasing the range would let that late completion land on a range already given to
the next container. The cost is one idle range for that container's life, reported as a warning.

## Authoritative references

- #730 acceptance 1-5.
  - Assignment: https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/730#issuecomment-6131408752
  - Ruling: https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/730#issuecomment-6131815815
  - Round 2: https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/730#issuecomment-6132404197
- Reviews R633-1 (https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/731#issuecomment-6132335284)
  and R632-1 (https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/731#issuecomment-6132397037).
- #532 (replay slots); `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` "Act-first local replication" and
  "Parallel replay slots".
- act 0.2.89:
  - `pkg/runner/runner.go`: per-job `NewParallelExecutor(maxParallel)` inside
    `NewParallelExecutor(ConcurrentJobs)`.
  - `pkg/model/workflow.go`: `GetMaxParallel` defaults to 4.
  - `pkg/runner/job_executor.go`: under `--rm`, each leg's container is removed before the
    worker takes the next leg.
- moby `daemon/update.go`: an update persists in a stopped container's configuration, and is
  applied before the response returns.

## How to get into the same state

```sh
git fetch origin
git switch 730-act-cpusets
git log --oneline dc4d06cb..HEAD
python3 -m pip install pyyaml
python3 -m pip install --require-hashes -r tools/markdown/requirements.txt
```

## How to validate

```sh
python3 scripts/act_ci.py --selftest
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --selftest
scripts/act_slot_proof.sh --selftest
python3 scripts/check_py_idiom.py
python3 scripts/check_py_idiom.py --selftest
python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --check
python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --selftest
python3 scripts/docs_check.py
python3 scripts/check_doc_style.py
python3 scripts/gen_toc.py --check
python3 scripts/gen_toc.py --verify-anchors
python3 scripts/check_em_dash.py --base dc4d06cb
python3 scripts/check_doc_paths.py
git diff --check dc4d06cb HEAD
```

Expected result / pass criteria: every command exits 0.

- The runner self-test ends `selftest: PASS`, with 490 `ok` arms and no `FAIL`.
- The CI contract reports 2016 items OK.
- The slot-proof self-test passes its 44 cases.
- The idiom ratchets hold: long function 9 <= 9, too many parameters 7 <= 7, over-long line 0.
- The em-dash gate reports 0 findings over 120 added lines.

Recorded with CPython 3.12.3 and PyYAML 6.0.3. The self-test also passes on CPython 3.14.7.

Post-merge measurement (acceptance 4, by the manager, per the ruling): the first `rtl-full`
replay on the merged runner, in the form of the recorded slot-0 replays (#721 at `42678ae2`,
#715 at `c7d0ad63`):

```sh
python3 -I <trusted-dev>/scripts/act_ci.py --pr <number> --sudo --workflow rtl-full
```

Read these lines:

1. The plan line above.
2. Per-job wall clock, from `[rtl-full/<job>] ⭐ Run Set up job` to
   `[rtl-full/<job>] 🏁  Job succeeded` (or `Job failed`). This needs per-line stamps, which act
   does not add.
3. `act-ci: rtl-full: CPU ranges: <n> job container(s) created: <m> seen on a range of their own
   by docker inspect, <g> removed before that, <s> never seen on one; at most <k> held a range at
   once`. Expect `m == n` (12 when the gate selects the full run), `g == 0`, `s == 0` and
   `k == 4`, with no `act-ci: WARNING: rtl-full: CPU ranges:` line.
4. The verdict, `act-ci: rtl-full: PASS at <sha>` or `FAILED (<rc>)`, against the before verdict
   at the same head.
5. On an isolated slot only, `act-ci: slot N: memory peak <x> GiB of its 24G cap; the cap was hit
   <h> time(s), with no OOM at it`.

## Known limitations / out of scope

- Not exercised against a live daemon in this lane: no replay, and no live self-test (ruling).
  No `docker events`, `docker container update` or `docker container inspect` has run. The first
  live run is the post-merge measurement, or `--interrupt-selftest` on slot 0 if the manager
  allows it before merge.
- The interrupt gate's requirement that its container be moved (R632-1's M18) is pinned only by
  that live gate.
- `--dry-run` is not daemon-free. In an isolated slot it starts the slot daemon and seeds the
  tool cache, which pulls the runner image. On slot 0 it creates the boundary on the default
  daemon. The dry-run lines above therefore come from the offline harness. Making `--dry-run`
  daemon-free is a separate change.
- A slot needs 20 CPUs where it needed 4. On a 128-CPU host, slots 1-5 fit any shipping
  workflow, and slot 6 fits workflows that derive one container. A host with fewer than 8 CPUs
  can no longer replay at all, slot 0 included (acceptance 1).
- A slot run by a pre-#730 runner can share CPUs with one run by this runner. Run every slot
  from one runner version.
- A container runs on its slot's staging range between its `create` and its move. `nproc`
  is 4 there too. Each container costs two more `docker container inspect` calls (after the
  move, and at `start`), so a burst of four creates is moved a little later than before. This is
  not measured.
- A move that cannot be confirmed keeps its range until the container is removed. With every
  range held, a further container stays on the staging range, as a warning.
- A workflow deriving more than 4 concurrent containers, or with an unreadable `max-parallel`,
  is refused. No shipping workflow does either.
- Acceptance 5 (`CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT` 2) is deferred to the post-merge measurement (ruling).
